Every REQ-NNN goal has multiple bound ACs both in requirements.md's Acceptance Criteria section and acceptance-tests.md's Requirement column. No orphaned goal found.

Round-1's missing-pointer defect on AC-026/TEST-026 is closed: requirements.md:520-529 now carries a 'Known-unsatisfied, do not read this criterion in isolation' pointer to OQ-004/Risks, and acceptance-tests.md:30 carries the matching 'integration (named SKIP until AC-009's pinned assert_terminal hash is formally amended)' Test Type plus an '(OQ-004)' pointer, correctly copying the two-part AC-036/AC-037 form as investigation.md:433-436 claims. But the remedy introduces a new, unaddressed contradiction: AC-034 (requirements.md:609-624) enumerates every allowlist-governed SKIP candidate -- AC-004, AC-007, AC-019-021, AC-036, AC-037, AC-042, AC-043, and 'any Context-present REQ-003 assertion' -- and AC-026 is deliberately excluded from that list (confirmed by investigation.md:438-442), and AC-026 is not itself a Context-present assertion, so it falls under no clause of AC-034 either. Meanwhile AC-035(b) (requirements.md:625-635) requires the suite to hard-fail -- never SKIP, never pass -- whenever 'any SKIP-shaped line in suite output does not match an allowlist entry (unknown SKIP)'. TEST-026 is now specified to emit exactly such a permanently un-allowlisted SKIP-shaped line until a human formally amends AC-009's hash. Neither requirements.md nor acceptance-tests.md states how TEST-026's own designed SKIP escapes AC-035(b)'s unknown-SKIP hard-fail, or scopes AC-035(b) to exclude it. A task author implementing TEST-035 literally from AC-035(b) and TEST-026 literally from its own row would build two suite behaviors that cannot both hold: either TEST-035 hard-fails the whole compatibility suite the instant TEST-026 legitimately SKIPs, or TEST-035 must silently special-case TEST-026 with no textual basis for doing so. This is a fresh defect introduced by the remedy itself. Separately, the appended precision correction to OQ-004/Risks is judged accurate -- 'always last' does hold (the emit is assert_terminal's final act) while the actually-violated clause is design.md's 'exactly once per round at the instant it evaluates' firing condition -- and appending rather than rewriting is an acceptable treatment here since each appended block explicitly supersedes 'the sentence/entry above' and AC-026's own point-of-use disclosure already uses the corrected framing, so a reader relying on AC-026 alone never sees the imprecise version.
